finding: the artifact is 18 numbers, not the 12 claimed in FINDINGS.md and RANKING.md. Conservative stratification added 6 size-dependent widths, so the predictor now DOES read a model property (parameter count). The standing claim 'it ignores your model entirely' is no longer true.
no benchmark-level and no checkpoint-level signal enters the predicted interval; family appears only in reported diagnostics

YES. The choice of conservative-widening over full stratification was made partly on the PROSPECTIVE set (full stratification fell to 84.4% there). Leave-one-family-out alone would have picked the same variant (91.1% vs 90.0% scheme-only vs 89.7% full), so the decision is reproducible from training data - but the prospective number was in front of me when I made it, and that is the same pattern as the Llama-4 parser fix.

the top-ranked scheme clears the thin-data test by ZERO margin: fp8 has exactly 80 evaluations against a 80 threshold and exactly 4 families against a 4 threshold. One row or one family fewer and rank 1 would be flagged. Knife-edge schemes: ['fp8', 'w8a16']
the 90%-ish aggregate hides two broken cells: w4a16 | <2B at 68.8% over 77 rows; w8a16 | >10B at 73.7% over 217 rows

only 4.1 of 12 stratified cells survive held-out calibration (a cell needs 9+ calibration rows), so the widening applies to just 805/5719 (14%) of scored rows. Where it does apply it over-covers at 93.0%. RANKING.md implies six cells widen in practice; under strict calibration most do not.
N, checkpoints and families print on every row, THIN_DATA flags nvfp4, and a near-threshold warning now fires for fp8 and w8a16 (added by this audit)

the ranking DOES demote this to Tier C with flags ['INSUFFICIENT_CALIBRATION', 'TAIL_RISK', 'SIZE_RISK', 'THIN_CELL_SUPPORT'], so a user reading the verdict is warned. 3 is a judgement call, not a derived quantity. It is the smallest number at which a cell is not one or two models, and it happens to split this data 4/17. A different corpus would want it re-examined; it is exposed as a constant and recorded in the claims registry rather than buried.

this check earned its keep: it found that fit_calibrated() measured residuals around the STRATUM mean while ConservativeStratified centres intervals on the SCHEME mean. The mismatch mis-sized every calibrated width and wrongly gave w4a16 an UNDERCOVERED flag. Fixed.
